result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md for WF02-REQ-020 (registration for an open event, atomic capacity enforcement, qr_token issuance) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-020, commit c1f02a7. Scope test: BACKEND-DEV's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts new, handlers/registration.ts new, handlers/start.ts modified with a real InlineKeyboard Register button replacing REQ-017's inert text CTA, i18n additions, index.ts new callback registration) is real behavioral surface -- a new live callback handler, a real button on an existing card, real registrations/audit_log/users writes. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, handlers/registration.ts, domain/event.ts's reused predicates (computeSeatsLeft/isRegistrationOpen/isFinished/getPendingSource/getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone), handlers/start.ts's resolveEventDeepLink/REGISTER_CALLBACK_PREFIX/buildRegisterCallbackData, docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md in full, the existing registration.test.ts (25 pure-function cases) and registration.db.test.ts (13 real-Postgres cases already covering AC1 at 20-iteration/2-way/capacity=1), the real i18n/en.ts registration.* catalog block (quoted verbatim in the spec), and both the REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER handoffs for this run (REVIEWER's own uncommitted 50-iteration/2-way and 20-iteration/5-way/capacity=2 races plus its raw pg_sleep lock-block proof; SECURITY-REVIEWER's S1-S14 full pass including the 'registerForEvent is the only insert(registrations) call site in the codebase' finding and its independent agreement with the S8/AC7 audit-both-outcomes reading) -- every fixture id, tg_id, and expected catalog string in the spec is grounded in a file actually opened, not guessed from the design doc's prose alone.

Each of the 7 acceptance criteria has at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case, and per this project's convention (REQ-019's precedent) none of them merely points at BACKEND-DEV's/REVIEWER's own already-extensive tests -- every case is this spec's own, with its own exact fixture values, and (the genuine gap found while reading) every one of them runs through the REAL callback handler chain via a real grammy.Bot dispatch, which no existing test -- committed or uncommitted, BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's -- has ever done; all prior tests call registerForEvent as a plain async function, never handlers/registration.ts's own makeRegisterCallbackHandler.

- AC1 (two concurrent registrations for the last seat): my own concurrency case is deliberately parameterized differently from every prior race so it is a genuinely independent stress configuration, not a repeat -- 30 iterations, 4 concurrent callers, capacity=3 (vs. BACKEND-DEV's 20/2-way/cap=1, REVIEWER's uncommitted 50/2-way/cap=1 and 20/5-way/cap=2), dispatched via Promise.all through the real register:<eventId> callback handler against fresh fixtures each iteration, asserting exactly 3 admitted + 1 waitlisted every single iteration.
- AC2 (registering twice): existing test only checks SEQUENTIAL double-registration -- added my own genuinely CONCURRENT same-user double-tap (Promise.allSettled racing the same tg_id against itself), checking exactly one row survives and neither dispatch throws an uncaught unique-violation (which would mean the lock, not just the DB constraint, failed to serialize the race).
- AC3 (qr_token >=128 bits CSPRNG): my own 5000-token (5x BACKEND-DEV's 1000) collision/structure test with different assertions than the existing one, not just a bigger N -- uniqueness, full 16-symbol hex-alphabet coverage (catches a broken encoder restricted to a subrange that a bare regex wouldn't), and a pathological-repeated-run sanity check.
- AC4 (closed/cancelled/finished): live dispatch checking the actual composed reply text verbatim against the real catalog strings (existing test only asserts outcome.kind), PLUS the exact registration_closes_at boundary instant via a real new Date() call in the live handler -- something no existing test exercises, since the committed fixture places the eval time a full day after the deadline, never AT it.
- AC5 (?start=e_<id>__linkedin -> source='linkedin'; no-pending_source fallback to 'direct'): full end-to-end live dispatch of /start -> consent:agree -> register, for both the channel-suffixed and bare-link cases, never calling setPendingSource/registerForEvent directly the way the existing test does.
- AC6 (requires_invite/requires_approval refusal): live dispatch checking verbatim refusal text and an explicit zero-rows read-back (existing test checks outcome.kind only).
- AC7 (exactly one audit_log row per write): live dispatch checking the audit row's action/payload/actor_user_id content and correct per-tapper attribution, not just row counts.

Added three cases beyond the 7 ACs, all named explicitly by this run's own instructions or found while reading the code: AC8 (capacity=0 event -> immediate waitlist, never admitted -- computeSeatsLeft(0,0)=0 is not >0), AC9 (a register callback naming a nonexistent event id -> the generic non-disclosure not-found reply, zero writes -- no existing test exercises this branch at all), and AC-card (the actual InlineKeyboard button's label/callback_data inspected directly from a live /start dispatch's captured reply_markup, plus confirming the old events.cardCta text is genuinely gone from the rendered card). Also included AC-schema (git diff --stat confirms REQ-020 introduces no migration, independently re-checking design section 10's own claim) and AC-catalog (i18n key-set parity across types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts's registration blocks, cardCta removal from all three, index.ts's actual callback registration line) as mechanical, non-dispatch checks.

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement explicitly in the spec's own execution-note section for TEST-RUNNER, and that AC1's/AC2's live-dispatch harness scripts must not run concurrently with any other DB-backed vitest file against the same scratch Postgres. Also noted explicitly why AC1's harness (unlike REQ-019's own AC1) does NOT need a real process kill+restart: REQ-020's atomicity property is about DB-transaction serialization via a row lock, not process-crash survival, so racing bot.handleUpdate() calls via Promise.all inside one process against the real Postgres connection pool is the correct and sufficient harness for this property -- a deliberate departure from REQ-019's precedent, stated so TEST-RUNNER does not wonder why no kill/restart step appears here.

Gap found while reading: none that blocks this spec. registration.test.ts and registration.db.test.ts correctly cover every pure-function rule-table cell and the domain-level DB behavior; the only gap is exactly the one this spec's cases close (nothing has ever dispatched a real callback_query through handlers/registration.ts). No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
